title: Relative representability of the normalizer of a smooth connected subgroup
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $G\to S$ be a smooth affine group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A group scheme over $S$ is a group object in schemes over $S$ [def-pc-scheme], with the multiplication, identity and inverse diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] over this base. Let $H\hookrightarrow G$ be a finitely presented closed subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion] which is smooth over $S$ with nonempty geometrically connected fibres [def-weil-connected-scheme]; geometrically connected means connected after extension to an algebraic closure of each residue field. For each $S$-scheme $W$, define $N(W)=\{g\in G(W):c_g(H_W)=H_W\}$, where $H_W=H\times_SW$, $c_g$ is conjugation by $g$, and equality is equality of closed subgroup schemes, or equivalently equality of subgroup functors on every $W$-scheme. Then $N$ is represented by a finitely presented closed subgroup scheme $N_G(H)\hookrightarrow G$. There is a canonical closed inclusion $H\hookrightarrow N_G(H)$. For every morphism $S\prime\to S$, the natural map $N_G(H)\times_SS\prime\to N_{G_{S\prime}}(H_{S\prime})$ is an isomorphism. No flatness or smoothness assertion about $N_G(H)$ is imposed.

source.place: Conrad, Proposition 2.1.6, printed pp.61--62; the normalizer functor and its closed finite-presentation representability. Base change follows from the displayed functor on all test schemes. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this relative group-scheme assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-connected-subgroup-noetherian-model] to obtain $A_0,G_0,H_0$ and the compatible base-change identifications. Work first over $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_0$; its group $G_0$ is affine and Noetherian. We construct the normalizer on all $S_0$-scheme tests, including non-Noetherian tests. Step 7 then pulls this construction back to $S$, so this reduction does not assume that the normalizer functor commutes with limits or is already represented.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.6, proof, p.62, noetherian reduction; Proposition 2.1.2, proof, p.57, descent of group data.

proof.text: Use the identity section $e:S_0\to H_0$. Write $H_0=\operatorname{Spec}B_0$ and $J=\ker(e^*:B_0\to A_0)$. By [lem-sfb-smooth-section-finite-jets], $D_n=\operatorname{Spec}(B_0/J^{n+1})$ is finite locally free for every $n\geq0$ and is the corresponding infinitesimal neighborhood after any base change. By [lem-sfb-smooth-section-universal-jet-density], if a closed subscheme of $(H_0)_T$ contains all $(D_n)_T$, it equals $(H_0)_T$, for every $S_0$-scheme $T$. The hypotheses hold because $H_0$ is affine, smooth and finitely presented, $A_0$ is Noetherian, and the fibers of $H_0$ are nonempty and geometrically connected. No assertion that $D_n$ is a subgroup is needed.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.6, proof, pp.62--63, neighborhoods of a section and their universal weak schematic density.

proof.text: For each $n$, restrict the two conjugation families to $D_n\times_{S_0}G_0$: they send $(h,g)$ to $ghg^{-1}$ and $g^{-1}hg$, respectively. These are morphisms by the multiplication and inverse morphisms in the group-object structure specified in the statement: compose $m$ twice with the projections and the inverse of the $G_0$ coordinate. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-locally-free-source-factorization-locus] with $D=D_n$, parameter scheme $P=G_0$, affine target $X=G_0$, and finitely presented closed target $Z=H_0$. It gives finitely presented closed subschemes $L_n^+,L_n^-\hookrightarrow G_0$. On every test $t:T\to G_0$, membership in $L_n^+$ means that conjugation by $t$ on $(D_n)_T$ factors through $(H_0)_T$, and membership in $L_n^-$ means the same for conjugation by $t^{-1}$.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.2, proof, p.60, Hom-functor coefficient equations pulled back along the orbit map; Proposition 2.1.6, proof, p.62.

proof.text: Write $G_0=\operatorname{Spec}C_0$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], write $L_n^\pm=\operatorname{Spec}(C_0/K_n^\pm)$ and set $I=\sum_{n\geq0}(K_n^++K_n^-)$ and $N_0=\operatorname{Spec}(C_0/I)$. An affine test factors through $N_0$ exactly when its ring map kills every $K_n^\pm$. For arbitrary tests this equivalence is checked on an affine open cover: the local quotient factorizations are unique and agree on overlaps, so they glue by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. For a test point $g\in G_0(T)$, the inverse image of $(H_0)_T$ under each map $c_g,c_{g^{-1}}:(H_0)_T\to(G_0)_T$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Step 2 says that it is the whole source precisely when it contains every $(D_n)_T$. Thus $N_0(T)$ consists exactly of $g$ satisfying both $c_g((H_0)_T)\subseteq(H_0)_T$ and $c_{g^{-1}}((H_0)_T)\subseteq(H_0)_T$. Applying $c_g$ to the second containment gives the reverse of the first. Hence $N_0$ represents the equality normalizer on all tests.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.6, proof, p.62, intersection of finite-source containment conditions; two-sided containment identifies the equality normalizer without using an endomorphism-surjectivity theorem.

proof.text: Since $G_0$ is Noetherian, [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth] makes $C_0$ a Noetherian ring. By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I$ is finitely generated. The morphism $G_0\to S_0$ is locally of finite presentation, so [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] gives that $C_0$ is a finitely presented $A_0$-algebra. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-quotient-fg-ideal] to $C_0$ and $I$: $C_0/I$ is finitely presented over $A_0$. Thus $N_0\to S_0$ is finitely presented. Also $C_0/I$ is presented over $C_0$ by the finitely many generators of $I$, with zero algebra generators, so $N_0\hookrightarrow G_0$ is a finitely presented closed immersion.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.2, proof, p.57, finite presentation over the noetherian model; Stacks 01OW (properties-lemma-locally-Noetherian), 00FM (algebra-section-Noetherian), 01TQ (morphisms-lemma-locally-finite-presentation), and 00F3 (algebra-definition-finite-type).

proof.text: For every $T$, equality $c_g((H_0)_T)=(H_0)_T$ is preserved under multiplication and inverse: $c_{gg'}=c_g\circ c_{g'}$, $c_1=1$, and $c_{g^{-1}}=c_g^{-1}$. These identities show that multiplication, identity and inverse of $G_0$ restrict to the represented subfunctor $N_0$. The Yoneda bijection [lem-pc-yoneda] turns these restrictions into scheme morphisms; their composites satisfy the group diagrams because their composites in $G_0$ do, and a closed immersion is monic by [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed]. For every $h\in H_0(T)$, subgroup closure gives $hH_0(U)h^{-1}=H_0(U)$ for every $T$-scheme $U$, so $H_0\to G_0$ factors canonically through $N_0$. If $H_0=\operatorname{Spec}(C_0/K)$, this factorization says $I\subseteq K$. Its map $C_0/I\to C_0/K$ is surjective, so [def-weil-closed-immersion] makes $H_0\to N_0$ closed. This proves the closed subgroup and inclusion assertions.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.6, p.61, normalizer as a closed subgroup; group-object operations and the canonical subgroup inclusion checked on all test schemes. Yoneda: Stacks 001P.

proof.text: Define $N=N_0\times_{S_0}S$. It is closed in $G$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. On affine coordinates, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition](1) preserves the finite presentations of both $N_0\to S_0$ and $N_0\to G_0$. The group operations and $H\to N$ are the base changes of those of Step 6. For any $S$-scheme $T$, its base change from the model satisfies $(H_0)_T=H_T$ and $(G_0)_T=G_T$, with identical conjugation operations. Thus Step 4 identifies $N(T)$ with the functor in the statement. For any $S'\to S$ and any $S'$-scheme $T$, exactly the same identifications give $(N\times_SS')(T)=N(T)=N_{G_{S'}}(H_{S'})(T)$. These bijections are natural. Yoneda [lem-pc-yoneda], or evaluation of these inverse transformations on the identity points, gives the claimed canonical isomorphism, commuting with the inclusions in $G_{S'}$. This verifies arbitrary, possibly nonflat and nonreduced, base change.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.6, proof, pp.62--63, construction on all tests and return from the noetherian model; Stacks 01QR, 05G5 and 001P for base change and Yoneda.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q10-d0633cbf9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read Conrad's Reductive group schemes from the public PDF (not in literature/): Prop 2.1.2 and Lemma 2.1.3 on pp.56-60, Prop 2.1.6, Def 2.1.7 and Example 2.1.10 on pp.61-63. The item statement is unchanged from the base and matches Prop 2.1.6 with Y=Y'=H over an affine base: equality normalizer, no flatness asserted. Steps: (1) noetherian model, with the transfer back done on all tests in step 7. (2) Finite jets and universal density: all hypotheses hold for H_0. (3) Factorization loci for the conjugations by g and by g^-1, with D_n finite locally free, P=X=G_0 affine fp, Z=H_0 fp closed. (4) I is the sum of the ideals K_n^±. Density turns jet containment into c_g(H_T)⊆H_T, the g^-1 containment gives equality, and non-affine tests glue. (5) C_0 Noetherian, so I is finitely generated and C_0/I is fp over A_0. (6) Subgroup structure by Yoneda, closed immersions are monic, and H_0⊆N_0 because I⊆K. (7) Base change to S and S' by Yoneda. Each cited statement says what is used. All off-unit citations are Mathlib leaves declared in tool_uses; I accept them. New nodes: all four statements are true and self-contained, statement-only and unsplit, with searches recorded. The noetherian model holds by EGA IV 17.8.7, 9.7.9 and 8.3.4. The finite jets hold for any ring since B=A⊕J. Universal density holds for arbitrary T: Conrad proves the local case on p.63, and I extended it by localizing at primes of R and covering T by affines. Small cases: A^1, G_m, and a disconnected counterexample showing connectedness is needed. The factorization locus is pp.59-60. Note: lem-pc-hilb-containment-locus (Stacks 0B97) is a near-duplicate of lem-sfb-finite-locally-free-source-factorization-locus but assumes constant degree and has no fp clause, so the new node stays; its stage-1 split should cite that node or lem-pc-affine-containment-ideal. No duplicates were found for the other three nodes. Minor: the report says source.place was corrected to include p.63, but only proof_origin.place was changed; this is harmless.
